correctness.rationale: CRT reduces support to one nonzero p-power component; minimal truncated p-adic value valuation divides every coefficient in an integral Newton basis. For odd p, the reduced nonzero degree<=2 polynomial function has nonzero proportion at least (p-2)/p by degree-two Schwartz-Zippel; for p=2, residue low bits turn Newton basis into a Boolean quadratic with support >=1/4 for n>=2 and an affine polynomial with support >=1/2 for n=1. Modulus 2 is separately handled as an ordinary integer polynomial. Explicit scalar-CRT witnesses attain the minimum over p|m for all m>=2,n>=1, nonzero polynomial *functions*; no complete zero-count spectrum claimed. Independent exhaustive small cases (2,2),(3,2),(4,2),(5,1),(6,1) agree; the larger 450011-vector packaged test was read but not independently repeated.
